issues.description: The datasheet reports article collection beginning 2022-12-01, while the supplied helper sets a June 2022 start and the Stata sample divides pre/post-GPT articles. The completeness and construction of the June–November 2022 pre-period are unverified.

The active helper reads and merges all three distinct prepared text outputs; no registered producer establishes tokenization, specificity/structure features, LM scoring, NER, or completeness. Originality.ai Lite 1.0.0, Stanford NER 4.2.0, and the reported Loughran–McDonald 2011 dictionary are provenance only when their outputs are supplied; exact versions are conditional prerequisites only if those outputs must be regenerated.

The dependency registry names Compustat_QFincls2.csv, Ad_exp.csv, and First_compustat_year.csv in SA_setup.py; the safe source view withholds parts of financials(), so their exact products, fields, and periods cannot be verified. Treat the gaps as unread coverage, not absent code or access denial.

Notebook 2 and notebook 3 call CRSP_universe(), which reads CRSP_uni_wip.pkl; the only visible writer is commented in a separate rebuild function. Supply the prepared pickle, or use the optional documented rebuild branch; raw writer inputs are not independent delivery requirements when the pickle is supplied.

Notebook 2 separately and jointly requires CRSP_window_measures.csv and CRSP_window_measure2.csv; each only visible writer is inside a triple-quoted block. These are two distinct prepared workflow outputs, not alternatives and not additional raw-source requirements when both prepared files are supplied.

Notebook 2 marks analyst-history preparation as online work, encloses the I/B/E/S Detail producer and Firm_day_past_ana.csv writer in a triple-quoted block, then reads Firm_day_past_ana.csv actively. The prepared file is the active input; raw detail history is only needed if rebuilding it.

Notebook 3 actively reads SA_article_sample_uni.csv, but no producer for this prepared article universe appears in the registered program sources. The supplied identifier workbook is not a verified compatible dataset.

Notebook 3 actively reads two prepared second-level windows. Its raw TAQ and complete-NBBO cleaning/writers are commented and constitute optional producer paths. Request both prepared windows as the active inputs, or confirm a conditional raw rebuild; the raw feeds are not separate mandatory requirements when their prepared outputs are supplied.
The Stata appendix reads SA_intraday_trade.dta and SA_intraday_quote.dta, but no producer for either file appears in the registered sources. They remain author-prepared inputs with unknown schemas.

The datasheet says RavenPack was used for an article-timing variable, but the registered programs do not identify its table, fields, or transform. The local catalog hit is a category table with no matched fields, not a compatible event extract.

Notebook 1 and the support module map CIZ DlyCalDt to the daily date/trading calendar, and the support module merges the CRSP market file with the daily stock data. The exact CIZ return-column identity, market-return meaning/version, sample/look-back coverage, and compatibility with downstream abnormal-return windows are not established. Do not assume legacy DSI return equivalence.

We collected Seeking Alpha articles, including article contents, article attributes and author
characteristics, from Seeking Alpha website with a Python program. The articles are published
from December 1, 2022 through August 31, 2024. We collected the article data in October 2024.

We scanned each processed SA article individually using Originality.ai. The model we employ in
our study is Lite 1.0.0 model. We scanned the articles in October and November 2024.

evidence.description: The datasheet identifies commercial financial and market sources and a later Compustat variable supplement.

Compustat, CRSP, I/B/E/S, WRDS Intraday Indicator and Thomson/Refinitiv data

Thomson/Refinitiv to construct financial characteristics and outcome variables. We initially
downloaded the data in October and November 2024. In April 2025, we downloaded additional
Compustat variables, DLCQ (Debt in Current Liabilities) and DLTTQ (Long-Term Debt – Total),
to complement the previous data.
